title: Golden GPU image pipeline: version pinning, candidate→stable promotion, and automated rollback hooks
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Goal
Implement a golden GPU image lifecycle that is safe-by-default and operable during rollout:
- Version pinning at the pool/module level (no implicit "latest")
- Staged promotion pipeline (candidate → stable)
- Automated rollback hooks that react to readiness/validation failure spikes

Context
Provision-to-ready automation is reducing manual bring-up, but image drift (driver/CUDA/NCCL mismatch, kubelet/containerd settings) is still a primary source of nodes getting stuck in Validating/Quarantined. We need a controlled image release channel so we can:
- Roll out changes gradually by region/GPU type/pool
- Correlate failures to an image version quickly
- Roll back without emergency Terraform edits or ad-hoc instance modifications

Requirements / Acceptance Criteria
1) Version pinning
- Each Dedicated pool must specify an explicit image identifier and image channel (candidate|stable).
- Provisioning orchestrator must log the requested image version/channel and the realized image ID on instances.
- Terraform applies should fail fast if required variables/tags are missing.

2) Promotion model
- New image builds land as candidate by default.
- Promotion to stable is a deliberate action with an audit trail (who/when/what version).
- Stable promotion must be gated on passing validation gates (GPU health, driver parity, kube join, NCCL smoke, perf canary) in at least one canary pool.

3) Rollback automation
- Rollback triggers: if readiness/validation failure rate crosses threshold for a given image version/channel over a sliding window (see notes), automatically demote/stop rollout and revert pools on candidate to last-known-good.
- Rollback must be bounded: only affect pools opted into automated rollback (feature flag) and only within the rollout scope (region/GPU type).
- Rollback action must be observable (events + metrics) and reversible (manual override).

4) Operational visibility
- Operators can answer "what image is this pool using" and "what changed" from internal tooling.
- All channel changes must emit audit events for compliance/post-incident forensics.

Design Notes / Decisions
- "Candidate" and "stable" are logical channels mapped to concrete immutable image versions (e.g., AMI IDs / GCE image selfLinks). We do not reuse the same version string to point to new content.
- Pool-level pinning: image_channel + image_version (or image_id). Rollouts change pool config, not instances in place.
- Rollback should be triggered by the same signals used to gate readiness (validation artifacts + state transitions). We avoid bespoke health checks.
- Rollback is a control-plane action (flip pool image pointer) + Terraform source-of-truth alignment. To prevent thrash, include hysteresis/cooldown and require minimum sample size.

Implementation Plan
A) Image build outputs
- Update image pipeline to publish immutable versions with metadata: driver/CUDA/NCCL versions, build timestamp, git SHA of image recipe, CVE scan summary, and supported GPU SKUs.
- Store metadata in build artifacts index used by fleet tooling.

B) Terraform conventions + tags
- Add required tags/outputs for provisioning: pool_id, region, gpu_type, image_channel, image_version.
- Add validation in terraform modules to ensure explicit image pinning (no empty/default "latest").

C) Promotion workflow
- Candidate build promoted to stable via a gated workflow (Release Eng + Infra sign-off), following the rollout plan.
- Promotion writes audit event and updates the stable pointer in the image registry.

D) Rollback hook
- Implement rollback controller that watches time-to-ready / validation failure metrics by (region, gpu_type, image_version, image_channel).
- On trigger, set pool image_channel to stable (or last-known-good) and stop further candidate expansion.
- Emit events + create a Linear incident/task stub for follow-up if rollback executed.

Trigger thresholds (initial)
- Use a conservative trigger during early rollout to avoid flip-flopping:
  - Minimum N=20 nodes attempted on a version within 30 minutes
  - Validation failure rate > 15% OR Quarantine rate > 8% for that image_version
  - Cooldown: 2 hours after rollback before allowing re-promotion
- Final thresholds should align with ENG-4821 SLO/error budget decisions and SRE alert tuning.

Testing
- Unit tests for image registry pointer updates and audit log emission.
- Integration test: canary pool set to candidate, force a validation failure spike (simulate NCCL smoke test failure), verify automatic rollback and event emission.
- Disaster test: verify we can manually override (lock channel) during an incident.

Rollout
- Start with us-east A100 Dedicated canary pool only.
- Enable automated rollback feature flag only for canary pools in first week.
- Expand to additional pools/regions after validation flake rate is stable.

Risks / Mitigations
- Risk: noisy/flake validations cause rollback thrash. Mitigation: minimum sample size + cooldown + use quarantine rate rather than single-step flake.
- Risk: Terraform drift if control-plane flips image pointers. Mitigation: record changes and provide a generated "recommended terraform patch" / notification to release coordinator; keep Terraform as desired-state while control plane enforces safety during rollout.
- Risk: compliance concerns around mutable pointers. Mitigation: stable pointer changes are audited; image content remains immutable.

References
- Confluence: Golden GPU image build and rollbacks (process + policy)
- ADR-017 Readiness state machine (for authoritative failure signals)
- Provision-to-ready validation checklist draft (defines the gating validations)
- Rollout plan draft (candidate rollout stages + rollback criteria)

Deliverables
- Pool-level explicit pinning of image channel/version across IaC + orchestration
- Candidate→stable promotion workflow with sign-off and auditability
- Automated rollback hooks with bounded blast radius + operator override
- Operator-facing visibility: events, metrics, and pointers to dashboards/runbooks
acceptance_criteria: Dedicated pool definitions require explicit image_channel and image_version/image_id; plans fail if omitted
New image builds default to candidate and can be promoted to stable with an auditable action
Automated rollback can revert candidate pools to stable when failure rate exceeds threshold and minimum sample size is met
Rollback actions are observable (events + metrics) and have a manual override/lock
Operators can query: pool → channel/version and see change history
